readings.title: Office procedure: returning borrowed display samples
readings.summary: Quy trình mới giúp công ty theo dõi mẫu trưng bày được mượn, xử lý trường hợp hư hỏng và chuẩn bị mẫu cho khách hàng tiếp theo.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Our sales office keeps furniture samples that staff borrow for customer visits. These include fabric books, small wood panels, and two folding display stands. During the last month, three visits began late because a required sample was missing or had been returned to an unexpected cupboard. Nobody had taken the items permanently, but finding them required several calls. From next Monday, the office will use the procedure below. Its purpose is to make samples available when promised while keeping borrowing simple enough for staff who often leave early for appointments.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Before borrowing anything, check the sample calendar on the shared office page. Each item has its own number, which is printed on a yellow label. Reserve the item under that number and enter your customer visit date, departure time, and expected return time. A reservation covers travel as well as the meeting itself. If your visit ends at three but you expect to return at five, book until five. This helps the next borrower plan realistically and prevents a second appointment from depending on an item that is still in a car.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The sample cupboard will remain beside reception, where staff can collect items without entering the meeting rooms. Take a quick look at each item before leaving. If a label is missing, ask the office coordinator to identify the sample before you record the collection. Please do not replace an unavailable sample with a similar one without telling the colleague who arranged the visit. Two wood panels may look alike under office lights but represent different finishes. A convenient replacement could therefore give a customer the wrong impression of the available product.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: On return, put samples on the inspection shelf rather than directly inside the cupboard. The coordinator will check them each afternoon and move ready items back into their numbered spaces. Leave a short note if something needs attention, even when the problem seems small. A loose ring in a fabric book can be repaired quickly if somebody knows about it. Returning damaged items does not automatically mean the borrower must pay. The immediate priority is to stop another colleague from discovering the problem halfway through a customer presentation.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Sometimes a customer meeting runs longer than expected. If this changes your return time, update the calendar and contact the next borrower directly. A calendar change alone may be missed while that person is travelling. The coordinator can help arrange another suitable sample, but cannot promise that every finish has a spare. If there is no suitable alternative, the two borrowers should agree which customer visit can move. Please avoid making promises to customers until the new arrangement is confirmed; otherwise, a small internal delay may create two disappointed customers.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: For visits lasting several days, borrow a travel case as well as the samples. The cases have soft sections that keep the wood panels apart. They add weight, but staff who tested them found that the panels were easier to carry together. Each case contains a printed inventory card. Check that card before leaving the customer's office, especially when several people have handled the samples. It is easier to find a missing fabric book while everyone is still present than to ask a customer to search after the display has been packed away.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The coordinator will review the calendar every Friday to identify repeated difficulties. The first review will focus on items with frequent overlapping requests, rather than on how many items each employee borrows. The office may buy a second copy of a popular sample if the records show a clear need. However, extra copies also require storage and regular checks, so buying everything twice is not the starting plan. Staff should report visits they could not arrange because a sample was unavailable; an empty calendar entry would not show that lost opportunity.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: This procedure will run as a four-week trial. During the trial, reception will keep a paper collection sheet for staff who cannot open the shared page before departure. The coordinator will copy those entries into the calendar later that morning. At the end of the trial, staff will discuss whether the new steps prevented delays and whether any step took unnecessary time. Suggestions should describe a real situation and a possible improvement. The office wants a reliable borrowing system that fits normal work, so practical feedback will be more useful than a general request for fewer rules.

readings.summary: Thông báo về dịch vụ nhận hộp rau hằng tuần, gồm giờ nhận, cách đổi người nhận, xử lý món thay thế và thử nghiệm điểm nhận tại khu dân cư.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: The Meadow Lane community centre will become a collection point for Hill Farm's weekly vegetable boxes from next Thursday. Residents asked for this service because the farm's delivery van cannot stop at every building in the neighbourhood. The centre offered its covered entrance, which is easy to reach from the main road. This notice explains how the first six weeks will work. The service is optional, and residents order directly from the farm. Centre volunteers will organise collection, but they will not choose the contents or take payment for orders.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Boxes will be available between five and seven on Thursday evenings. The farm will place them on numbered tables, and each customer will receive a collection number by text that afternoon. Show the number to a volunteer, who will help you find the correct box. Please check the name on the label before leaving, since several households have similar surnames. Bring a strong bag if you intend to transfer the vegetables and leave the box behind. Empty boxes can be stacked beside the entrance for the driver to collect the following week.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The standard box contains five kinds of vegetables, but the exact selection depends on what the farm can supply that week. The order page will show a planned list on Monday. If an item becomes unavailable, the farm may replace it with another vegetable and explain the change in Thursday's message. Customers who strongly dislike a particular item can record one exclusion on their account. This is intended to make the box more useful, although it does not allow customers to build a completely individual order from the farm's full range.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: If you cannot collect your box, a friend or neighbour may collect it for you. Send that person your collection number and tell the farm their name before noon on Thursday. Volunteers will use the updated list at the entrance. Please arrange this yourself instead of asking volunteers to find someone willing to help. They need to remain at the tables during the collection period. A message in the neighbourhood chat may be useful, but avoid posting your collection number publicly; send it directly to the person who agrees to collect.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Boxes left after seven will go into a locked store room overnight. Customers can collect them from the centre office between nine and eleven on Friday morning. The centre cannot offer collection later on Friday because the room is needed for an afternoon activity. If neither collection period works for you, contact the farm before the weekly order deadline to discuss another arrangement. The centre has no chilled storage for these boxes. For that reason, the farm will only send vegetables that it considers suitable for the agreed collection schedule.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Please inspect your box when you get home and contact the farm if the contents differ from the label or an item appears damaged. Include your order number and a clear photograph when possible. The farm will discuss a replacement or a credit after reviewing the message. Volunteers cannot settle these requests at the collection tables, and opening every box there would slow the queue. However, tell a volunteer immediately if a box is wet or broken, so it can be moved away from the other orders and reported to the driver.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The trial also includes a simple way to reduce packaging. Customers may return clean, dry boxes at the next collection, provided the boxes still hold their shape. Remove any personal labels first. The farm will check returned boxes before using them again. Volunteers will record how many boxes come back, but they will not record which households return them. Some residents walk home in the rain or need the box for storage during the week, so the organisers want to understand the practical limits before introducing any reward for returns.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: After six collections, the farm and the centre will review attendance, late collections, and comments from customers and volunteers. The trial may continue, move to an earlier time, or stop if the arrangement causes too much work for the centre. Customers will receive a message before any change takes effect. During the trial, please keep the entrance clear and use the marked waiting area if a queue forms. Other visitors will still be entering the building for evening classes. A successful service needs to fit alongside those activities, rather than take over the whole entrance.

readings.title: Migration proposal: replacing a shared robot login
readings.summary: Đề xuất thay tài khoản tự động dùng chung bằng tài khoản riêng cho từng tác vụ, với kiểm kê, chạy thử, theo dõi và kế hoạch khôi phục.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Several scheduled jobs in our reporting service currently use one shared account called report-robot. The account downloads supplier files, prepares internal summaries, and uploads completed reports to customer folders. This arrangement was convenient when the service had only two jobs. It is now harder to understand because eleven jobs use the same login. When a report is missing, the activity history identifies the shared account but does not clearly identify the responsible job. This proposal recommends separate accounts for separate jobs, introduced gradually over three weeks to keep regular reporting available.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The immediate concern came from a failed customer upload last month. An engineer found several actions by report-robot around the failure, but had to compare three different job logs before locating the relevant one. Nobody found evidence of an unauthorised action. Nevertheless, the investigation showed that the shared identity made ordinary troubleshooting slower. The same account also has access to folders that some of its jobs never use. Separating the jobs would let us describe each account's purpose more clearly and limit its access to the resources required for that purpose.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Before creating replacement accounts, each job owner must complete an inventory sheet. The sheet asks which files the job reads, where it writes results, how often it runs, and who receives a failure notice. Owners should check the actual job configuration rather than copy an old design document. Two jobs have changed destination folders since those documents were written. The inventory will also identify jobs without an active owner. Those jobs will remain on the current account until someone accepts responsibility and confirms whether the work is still needed.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: We propose starting with the weekly stock summary because its inputs and destination are well understood. Its new account will read one supplier folder and write to one internal report folder. During the first trial, the new job will place its result in a separate comparison folder. The existing job will continue producing the report that staff use. The owner will compare both results and check the activity records. This adds temporary work, but it gives us evidence about the new setup before we change the normal destination or remove the old access.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Once the comparison is satisfactory, the owner will switch the stock summary to its normal destination and observe two scheduled runs. A successful file upload alone will not finish the check: the receiving team must confirm that it can open the report and that the contents are complete. If the trial fails, the owner will return the job to its previous account using the saved configuration. Other migrations will pause while the cause is investigated. We want a repeatable process, so a problem in the first job should improve the instructions for the remaining ten.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The proposal has costs as well as benefits. Separate accounts mean more records to maintain, and new staff will need a clear account list. We will name each account after its job and store the owner, purpose, and review date beside it. Account details will be kept in the team's existing protected configuration store. They should not appear in handover messages or ordinary issue comments. The plan uses tools already available to this team, but the additional administration still needs time in the migration schedule instead of being treated as free work.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Customer-facing uploads will move last because their destinations vary and a missed delivery affects people outside the company. Before each move, support will confirm the customer's expected report time and the contact to use if a delay occurs. We do not plan to ask customers to change their folders during this migration. If an existing destination cannot accept the new account, the owner will investigate it separately rather than extend the account's access to unrelated folders. A narrow, understood exception is easier to review than a broad change made simply to finish the schedule.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: The shared account will be retired only after every active job has moved and its owner has signed off. Engineers will then check for remaining activity before disabling it. The proposal does not promise that separate accounts will prevent every reporting failure; incorrect inputs or job logic can still cause problems. Its expected benefit is clearer responsibility and more appropriate access. After one month, the team will compare investigation time for new failures with the previous records. That review will help us judge whether the extra account maintenance has delivered the practical improvement we intended.

readings.title: Handover memo: preparing the monthly printing order
readings.summary: Bản bàn giao hướng dẫn tổng hợp nhu cầu in ấn, kiểm tra bản mẫu, quản lý chi phí và nhận hàng trong thời gian người phụ trách nghỉ phép.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: I will be away during the next monthly printing order, so this memo explains the work you will take over. The order includes course booklets, visitor maps, and feedback cards for our training centre. These items go to the same printer, but different colleagues approve their contents. Last month, we received the correct number of maps with an old room name on them. The printer had used the file we supplied, so the mistake began here. This handover focuses on choosing the right files and getting clear approval before production starts.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: On the first working day of the month, send the request form to the course coordinator, reception lead, and events assistant. Ask each person to provide an item name, quantity, required delivery date, and final file. The form closes on Wednesday at noon. If somebody sends a request only through chat, ask them to add it to the form so it stays with the rest of the order. You do not need to chase every possible requester. Contact the three named colleagues, then use the completed form as the main record.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Before requesting a price, compare the new quantities with the stock cupboard. Reception will help you count visitor maps and feedback cards; the course coordinator holds the booklet stock. We order enough for confirmed activities plus a small agreed reserve. Extra printing can reduce the price per copy, but unused items take up space and may become outdated. Last month's spare maps show why a cheaper copy is not always a useful saving. If a requested quantity seems unusually high, ask the requester for the reason instead of quietly reducing it yourself.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Create a separate order folder and place only approved files inside it. Keep draft versions in their original team folders. Each approved filename should include the item and month, such as visitor-map-june. Open every file to check that it matches the form; a correct filename does not prove the contents are correct. For booklets, confirm the page order and whether any blank pages are intentional. For maps, ask reception to check room names and entrance details. You are checking that the right version reached the folder, while the named colleague remains responsible for approving the information.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Send the printer the quantities and approved files together, and request a written quotation showing printing, packing, and delivery separately. This makes it easier to compare the quotation with the monthly budget. The printer sometimes offers a faster service at an additional cost. Use that option only if the normal delivery date would miss a confirmed activity and the centre manager approves the extra amount. A late internal request does not automatically justify faster printing. First ask whether existing stock or a small temporary handout could cover the immediate need.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The printer will send a digital proof before producing the order. Forward each proof to the colleague responsible for that item and give a clear response deadline. Approval must be recorded in the order folder. If the colleague finds an error, send one complete list of corrections to the printer rather than several separate messages. After a correction, request an updated proof. Do not assume that fixing one room name means every other detail has stayed the same. Compare the changed version with the approved source file before giving permission to print.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Delivery usually arrives at reception in labelled cartons. Ask reception to keep the cartons together until you can compare them with the delivery note. Count the packs, open one pack of each item, and check the printed version. If something is missing or different, photograph the label and a sample, then contact the printer with the order reference. Put questionable items on the hold shelf so colleagues do not use them by mistake. Correct items can be distributed immediately, provided their quantities and destinations are recorded in the order folder.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: At the end of the order, save the quotation, approvals, delivery note, and any problem messages together. Add a short note about actual delivery time and leftover stock. This will help next month's coordinator estimate quantities and spot repeated difficulties. You can ask the centre manager about spending decisions while I am away, and reception can explain where supplies belong. Please do not wait for my return if a delivery problem needs a prompt response. The handover is complete when the items are checked, the records are saved, and the next coordinator can understand what happened.

readings.title: Service estimate: a suitcase that will not roll straight
readings.summary: Cửa hàng giải thích nguyên nhân vali kéo lệch, so sánh các phương án sửa, chi phí và lịch hoàn thành trước chuyến đi của khách.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Thank you for bringing your medium-sized suitcase to our repair counter on Monday. You explained that it pulls to the left when you walk through a station and sometimes makes a scraping sound. You also told us that your next trip begins on Saturday morning. We inspected the suitcase without removing its lining or replacing any parts. This estimate describes what we found and the options available. Please read the timing section before choosing a repair, because the cheapest option is useful only if the suitcase is ready when you need it.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The rear left wheel does not turn as freely as the other three wheels. We found thread wrapped around its centre and wear along one edge. After removing the thread, the wheel turned more easily, but the suitcase still pulled left during our short floor test. The handle opened and closed normally, and the main zip worked during inspection. One corner of the outer case has a surface scratch. We have included that detail in our record, although it did not appear to affect the way the suitcase moved in the test.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Our first option is to replace only the worn wheel with an available compatible part. The price is 280,000 dong, including fitting and a final floor test. This wheel is the same size as the original, but its grey colour will differ from the remaining black wheels. We can complete this option by Thursday afternoon if you approve it by Tuesday at noon. The repair is aimed at the pulling problem. It will not remove the surface scratch, change the handle, or make an older suitcase look like a new one.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The second option is to replace both rear wheels with a matching pair ordered from our supplier. This costs 460,000 dong, including fitting. A matching pair would give the rear of the suitcase a more consistent appearance, which some customers prefer. However, the supplier expects the parts to reach us on Friday, and we cannot promise completion before your Saturday departure. The right rear wheel currently passed our inspection, so replacing it is a choice rather than a repair we consider necessary. Please weigh the appearance benefit against the timing and extra cost.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: You also asked whether cleaning all four wheels would be enough. We can provide that service for 90,000 dong and return the suitcase on Wednesday. Cleaning may remove dirt and loose material, but our inspection suggests it would not correct the worn edge on the left wheel. If you choose cleaning alone, we will test the suitcase afterwards and tell you how it moves. You could then approve a wheel replacement, although that later decision might miss the Thursday completion slot. We would not describe cleaning as a confirmed solution to the pulling problem.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: If you approve a wheel replacement, we will contact you if removing the old part reveals damage that was hidden during the inspection. Any additional work requires a new estimate and your agreement. We will not automatically add it to the bill. Sometimes the surrounding fitting is weaker than it appears from outside, and we prefer to explain that before continuing. If you decide against further work, we will discuss whether the original part can be put back. This estimate covers the visible problem, not every possible condition inside the suitcase.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: At collection, please allow ten minutes to try the suitcase on the shop floor. Bring a few ordinary travel items if you want to test it with some weight inside. We will show you the replaced part and explain what work was completed. Keep the receipt, which includes the repair date and the part fitted. If the new wheel develops a problem within our stated thirty-day service period, contact the shop with that receipt. We will inspect the repaired area before deciding what action is appropriate; unrelated damage would need a separate discussion.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Based on your departure date and the current condition of the other wheels, we recommend the single-wheel replacement. It offers a practical repair within the available time, provided approval arrives before the deadline. Please reply with your chosen option and a telephone number we can use during the work. You may also collect the suitcase without approving a repair; there is no inspection charge for this estimate. If travel plans change, tell us before parts are ordered. That may make the matching-pair option more convenient, but it does not change what our initial inspection found.

readings.title: Release plan: previewing changes before a bulk update
readings.summary: Kế hoạch phát hành tính năng xem trước khi cập nhật hàng loạt, làm rõ phạm vi áp dụng, cách xử lý dữ liệu thay đổi và tiêu chí mở rộng thử nghiệm.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Our inventory application lets store managers change the location of many products in one action. This saves time when a shop reorganises its shelves, but the current screen moves directly from product selection to confirmation. Support has received requests for a clearer view of what will change. One manager selected products from two branches while intending to update only one. She noticed the mistake after saving and corrected the records manually. This release will add a preview step so managers can inspect the proposed changes before applying a bulk location update.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The preview will show each selected product's name, branch, current location, and proposed location. A summary above the table will state the total number of products and the branches included. Managers can return to the selection screen without losing the location they entered. The design deliberately keeps the branch column visible on smaller screens, even though that leaves less room for long product names. During interviews, managers said a shortened name was easier to handle than a hidden branch, because the branch often determined whether an update was appropriate.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The preview is a planning view, not a reservation of the records. Another employee may edit a product while the manager is reviewing the table. When the manager presses Apply, the application will check whether each selected record still matches the version used for the preview. Changed records will be left untouched and listed separately. The remaining records can be updated. This choice avoids replacing a colleague's recent change without warning, but it means a bulk action may finish with fewer updates than the preview originally showed.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: The result screen must therefore explain partial completion clearly. It will show how many products changed and how many were skipped, with a link to the skipped list. The message will use ordinary wording rather than ask managers to understand record versions. Managers can review skipped products and start a new action if the proposed location is still suitable. We considered stopping the whole update whenever one record changed, but several managers said that would delay useful work on hundreds of unaffected products. The chosen approach preserves progress while making exceptions visible.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Before development finishes, the quality team will prepare cases involving one branch, several branches, and products with long names. It will also arrange a second account to edit selected products during preview. The tests must confirm both the updated records and the records that should remain unchanged. Checking only the success message would miss an important part of the feature. A separate usability session will ask managers to explain the preview in their own words. If they believe the preview guarantees every displayed update, the wording will need revision before release.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The first release will be available to five volunteer stores for one week. Their managers already use bulk location updates regularly and have agreed to report confusing steps. Support will provide a short illustrated guide showing selection, preview, and results. The guide will also explain that returning to selection is a normal part of checking an update. We will record how often managers leave the preview without applying changes, but that number alone will not count as failure. It may show that the new step helped someone catch an unwanted selection.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: During the trial, engineers will compare the action records with the result counts shown to managers. Any disagreement will pause expansion until the cause is understood. Support will collect examples of unclear messages without asking stores to send private product details in ordinary chat. If a serious problem appears, the team can switch trial stores back to the previous screen. That switch changes the interface for future actions; it does not reverse updates already completed. For a mistaken completed action, support will use the existing investigation process and examine the available history.

We will introduce the preview to another group of stores before making it the standard screen. This release does not add a general undo button or change who can move products. readings.title: Workplace agreement: protecting the afternoon focus period
readings.summary: Nhóm dịch vụ thử nghiệm giờ làm việc tập trung buổi chiều, phân công người trực yêu cầu khẩn cấp và đánh giá tác động đến tiến độ cùng chất lượng phục vụ.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Our customer services team will test a daily focus period from two to three thirty for the next month. During that time, most team members will work on tasks that require sustained attention, such as preparing complex replies or checking account histories. The idea came from a team discussion about unfinished work. People were answering quick questions throughout the afternoon, then completing longer tasks after normal hours. The trial is intended to give those tasks a predictable place in the day while keeping a clear route for customers who need a prompt response.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: The focus period does not close the service desk. Two colleagues will remain on the response rota each afternoon, covering the shared inbox and the telephone. Their names will appear on the team calendar by the previous Friday. The rota will change daily so the same people do not always lose their focus time. Colleagues on the rota can take their own focus period earlier that day, after agreeing a suitable time with the team lead. This arrangement requires planning, but it spreads both the service responsibility and the benefit of uninterrupted work.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Before two, each person should choose one main task and collect the information needed to begin it. Write a short status message showing that you are in the focus period and when you will check ordinary messages again. You do not need to describe private customer details in that message. If your task requires input from another department, request it earlier rather than waiting until the focus period starts. The aim is to reduce avoidable interruptions, not to spend ninety minutes waiting for a reply that could have been requested in the morning.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Urgent matters should go to the colleagues on the response rota first. For this trial, an urgent matter is one that blocks a customer's scheduled activity that afternoon or requires a same-day action with an approaching deadline. A general request for information is not urgent merely because the sender writes the word urgent. The rota colleague will collect the basic facts and decide whether to interrupt a specialist. If an interruption is necessary, the message should explain the problem, the deadline, and the specific help required, so the specialist can respond without a long exchange.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Ordinary internal questions can be placed in the team channel for later attention. Please use a clear subject and include enough context for someone to answer when they return. Avoid sending the same question privately to several people; that creates several interruptions and may produce conflicting answers. At three thirty, team members will check messages before starting their next activity. If a question remains unanswered by the time its information is needed, contact the team lead. The focus period should make communication more organised, rather than leave colleagues uncertain about whether anyone has seen their request.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Meetings should normally be arranged outside the focus period. However, we will keep two existing customer meetings that cannot move during the first week. The people attending those meetings may choose another focus time with the team lead. We will record these exceptions to see whether the proposed time fits our actual workload. Cancelling useful meetings simply to achieve a perfect calendar would miss the purpose of the trial. If exceptions become frequent, the team may need a different daily time or a shorter focus period instead of asking everyone to work around an unsuitable arrangement.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: At the end of each week, staff will report whether their chosen tasks progressed and whether they still worked late to finish them. The lead will also check customer response times and unresolved requests. We will count necessary interruptions, but we will not rank individual staff by that number. Some roles naturally receive more difficult questions than others. A useful review needs to consider the work behind the numbers. Staff may include a brief example of a prevented delay or a task that benefited from concentration, without naming the customer involved in the example.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: After four weeks, the team will decide whether to continue, adjust, or end the arrangement. We need evidence that longer tasks move forward without creating unreasonable delays for customers or colleagues. The agreement can change if the trial reveals a better way to balance those needs. In the meantime, please treat a colleague's focus status as a real work commitment and use the agreed route for urgent help. The trial is a shared scheduling decision, so nobody should have to defend their concentration time separately every afternoon. Clear expectations will make the experiment easier to judge.

readings.summary: Thông báo thử nghiệm quy trình lên phà mới vào sáng thứ Bảy để hành khách mang nhiều hàng có thể sắp xếp đồ mà không cản lối đi.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: From Saturday, the Riverside ferry will test a new boarding arrangement on its busy morning crossings. Many passengers use the ferry after visiting the market and carry large shopping bags or small folding trolleys. Recently, crew members have spent extra time moving these items away from the central walkway before departure. The ferry operator wants to reduce that delay while making boarding less confusing. This notice explains the trial for passengers travelling between Riverside Market and West Quay. The crossing timetable and normal ticket prices will remain the same during the trial.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: At Riverside Market, passengers with trolleys or more than two large bags should wait in the blue marked area beside the ticket booth. Other passengers should use the usual queue. A crew member will invite the blue-area passengers forward first so they can place their belongings in the marked storage spaces. This is a boarding arrangement, not a separate ticket category. People waiting in the blue area still need an ordinary ticket. Please avoid joining that area simply to board earlier if you are carrying only a small shoulder bag.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The storage spaces are beside the rear seating area and are marked with white lines. Put your bags fully inside a marked space and keep handles from extending into the walkway. Trolleys should be folded where their design allows it. Crew members can explain where to place items, but passengers remain responsible for moving their own shopping. If you need assistance, tell the ticket clerk before boarding so the crew can discuss what help is available. Waiting until departure to mention a difficult item may leave too little time to make a workable arrangement.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: There is room for six folding trolleys on each crossing. When those spaces are full, the crew may ask another passenger with a trolley to wait for the next ferry. They will explain the reason before that passenger boards. Bags must not be placed across empty seats to create extra storage. Seats are intended for passengers, and the number needed can change as people board. If your shopping is unusually bulky, contact the ferry office before your journey. Staff can discuss a quieter crossing, although they cannot reserve a trolley space in advance.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Keep small valuables with you instead of leaving them among shopping bags. Please also make sure that containers are closed and cannot easily spill when placed on the floor. If something leaks, tell a crew member rather than trying to hide it under another bag. The crew may need to move nearby items and clean the area before departure. We know that passengers want to get home quickly, but ignoring a spill usually creates more work later. The trial depends on keeping the shared space usable for everyone throughout the short crossing.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: At West Quay, passengers without stored bags will leave first. Passengers using the storage spaces should remain seated until a crew member invites them to collect their belongings. This gives them more room to unfold trolleys and organise their shopping. Check that you have all your bags before walking up the exit ramp. If you discover a missing item afterwards, contact the ferry office with the crossing time and a description. Crew members will bring unclaimed items to the office after checking the ferry, rather than leave them on board for the next trip.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: The trial will apply to Saturday departures from eight until noon for four weeks. Afternoon crossings will continue with the existing boarding process. Staff will record departure delays, the number of passengers asked to wait, and comments about the two waiting areas. They will also watch whether early boarding gives people enough time to store their belongings without rushing. A shorter delay would be useful, but it would not by itself prove that the arrangement works well. The operator also needs to know whether passengers can understand and follow the instructions easily.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Passengers can give feedback through a short form at either ticket booth or by contacting the ferry office. Please mention the date and approximate crossing time so staff can connect your comment with the trial records. Useful comments include places where signs were difficult to see or instructions arrived too late. At the end of four weeks, the operator will decide whether to continue or change the arrangement. Any permanent change will be announced at both terminals before it begins. For now, listen to the crew and allow a little extra time on your first journey using the new queues.

readings.title: Support exchange: an import with unexpected empty fields
readings.summary: Chuỗi trao đổi hỗ trợ làm rõ vì sao nhập danh mục sản phẩm thành công nhưng mất nội dung ghi chú, rồi hướng dẫn nhập lại có kiểm soát và cải thiện cảnh báo.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Customer message, Monday 08:40: We imported our updated product catalogue yesterday, and the application reported that all 240 rows were accepted. The product names and prices look correct, but the delivery notes are empty on many records. Those notes explain things such as collection days and packaging choices, so our sales team uses them regularly. We have paused further imports until we understand what happened. I have attached the file we used and a screenshot of the result message. Please tell us whether the missing notes can be restored without changing the prices again.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Support reply, Monday 09:15: Thank you for sending the file and explaining which information matters to your team. Please keep the original file unchanged while we investigate. We will first compare its column headings with the import settings saved on your account. Could you also confirm whether the notes were present before yesterday's import? We can see that the rows were accepted, but that result does not show which source column supplied each field. We will avoid asking you to repeat the whole import until we can explain the likely effect of doing so.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Customer reply, Monday 09:50: The notes were present before the import. Our supplier changed the spreadsheet layout this month, and the column previously called Delivery note is now called Fulfilment message. I assumed that choosing the saved import setup would still connect the information correctly. I noticed an empty choice beside the delivery-note field on the mapping screen, but thought that meant the existing notes would remain. The preview showed product names and prices, which I checked carefully. I did not open the additional-fields section because those first columns appeared to be correct.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Support reply, Monday 11:10: We have reproduced the behaviour using an invented catalogue with the same headings. The saved setup matched the unchanged name and price headings, but did not match the renamed notes heading. In your selected update mode, an unmapped delivery-note field is treated as an empty value. That explains why the existing notes became empty even though the rows were accepted. The result message counted accepted rows rather than confirming that every field contained information. We agree that the current screen did not make this distinction clear enough before you applied the update.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Support instructions, Monday 11:25: The attached source file still contains the notes, so we can use it for a controlled repair. Create a new import setup and connect Fulfilment message to the application's delivery-note field. Select the mode that updates only the fields you explicitly map. Map the product code and delivery-note fields, leaving the price field outside this repair. The product code identifies which existing record receives each note. Before applying anything, open the full preview and check several examples, including a product with a long note and one whose source note is genuinely empty.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Customer reply, Monday 13:05: We tried the repair first with five products in a separate test catalogue. Four received the expected notes, and the fifth stayed empty because its source cell was empty. Their prices remained unchanged. We then prepared the complete repair and asked a second colleague to review the mapping and preview. She found one product code with an extra space at the end. We corrected that cell in a copy of the source file and checked the preview again. The application now shows the expected matches, so we are ready to apply the repair.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Support follow-up, Monday 14:00: After applying the repair, please check records in the normal product view as well as the import result page. Keep the repair file and its saved setup together so the next person can understand how the columns were connected. For future supplier files, compare headings before reusing this setup. A saved setup reduces repeated work, but it should not replace a check when the source layout changes. We have also recorded a product request for a warning when this update mode would empty an existing field because no source column is mapped.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Customer closure, Tuesday 09:00: We completed the repair yesterday afternoon and checked a sample with the sales team this morning. The delivery notes are back, and the prices match the values from Sunday's import. We have added a short import checklist to our team folder, including a check of all mapped fields and a second review when supplier headings change. Please keep us informed about the proposed warning. For now, the explanation of update modes is enough for us to continue working, and we have asked one colleague to maintain the saved setups instead of leaving that responsibility unclear.
